statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail eases to 24% back into the watch band after NQ futures retraced roughly 60 points off a fresh 30,370.00 session low, with the 2-year flat near 4.90% and Brent easing from above $105.
recommendation: Tail steps back one point below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping yields WATCH rather than BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. The change reflects an observed retracement off the session extreme together with a flat 2-year and easing crude, which removes two of the four amplifiers that were aligned an hour ago. The evidence-based danger window narrows to 12:00-16:00 UTC, covering the Barkin speech, the 12:30 UTC claims release, the 13:30 UTC cash open and the early-afternoon data. Observed opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks would argue for a higher Tail than published; a genuine two-way open would argue for a lower one.
headline: NQ retraces about 60 points off a fresh session low as the front end flattens and crude eases
body: NQ futures trade near 30,430, down roughly 1.1% from the 30,764.75 previous close, after printing a fresh session low at 30,370.00 during this hour. Two independent quote sources agree on the level and on the 30,370.00 low. The single most important change since the previous assessment is what followed that low: price has recovered about 60 points from it, so NQ is no longer holding within a few points of a session extreme it had just re-set. An hour ago the pattern was repeated extension after a failed retracement; the same structure now shows a retracement that has been rewarded, which is the specific behaviour the block-band reading was pricing against. The driver remains duration rather than equity-specific news, and the level of that driver is unchanged: the US 10-year holds about 5.14%, its highest since July 2007, after a weak five-year auction and S&P Global PMI data showing multi-year highs in input and output price inflation. Two details qualify it. The 10-year is adding only about 3 basis points today against far larger prior daily moves, and the 2-year is flat near 4.90%, so the front end is not extending the hawkish repricing even though futures now price roughly a 70% chance of an October increase against 50% a week ago. Energy is also stepping back rather than reinforcing, with Brent at $104.74, up 1.6%, and WTI at $93.23, up 1.2%, both below the levels recorded an hour earlier as US-Iran talks stay unresolved. VIX is the one amplifier still extending, at 16.39 against a 15.18 close, a gain of 8.0%, with a 16.57 session high, though that remains a low absolute level. Of the four amplifiers aligned an hour ago, two have stopped extending and one has partially retraced, which is why Tail eases by a point rather than pushing further into the block band. Stress stays elevated because the multi-decade-high yield level, Japanese yields at a 1996 high after the overnight rout, and crude above $100 all persist regardless of intraday structure. Yesterday's cash session traded a 30,353.88-30,706.23 range in the Nasdaq-100 and closed at 30,470.29, above its low, so the current futures low sits just below a level where retracement was still being rewarded at the last close. Shared Finviz context was read at the start of this run but was collected at 06:48 UTC, making it roughly 224 minutes old, and was marked partial with futures and calendar sections unavailable. Under the supporting-evidence contract it is stale, so no part of it was used as evidence and all figures above come from independent current sources. The structural checkpoints ahead are the 12:00 UTC Fed Barkin speech, jobless claims at 12:30 UTC against a 201K consensus, the 13:30 UTC US cash open, new home sales at 14:00 UTC near a 615K consensus and the Kansas City Fed index at 15:00 UTC.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry published Claude assessments. Tail ran 12-15% through the European and early US hours of Sep 23 in a normal-to-mixed regime, printed 25% for the 14:00 UTC hour as the post-PMI bond leg developed, then held 20-24% through the US afternoon and the Asian session. It eased to 17-19% between 01:00 and 03:00 UTC, printed 22% at 04:00 UTC on a brief trend-down read, and closed the window at 24% and 25% for the 08:00 and 09:00 UTC hours as the duration move re-accelerated into a fresh session low. Stress was the more persistent signal, rising from the mid-30s to 57% at 18:00 UTC, easing to around 50% overnight and returning to 57-58% for the final two slots. Confidence held in the 84-88% band throughout.
outlookSummary: The published path holds Tail at 24% in the watch band for the current and next hour, then steps into the block band at 25-26% from 12:00 through 15:00 UTC, peaking across the claims reaction and the cash open, which defines the evidence-based danger window. It returns to the watch band at 23% from 16:00 UTC, decays through the US afternoon and evening to 19-20% by the Asian session, and drifts back to 20-21% across the following European hours as the amplifier stack is assumed to unwind slowly. Stress follows the same shape at a higher level, peaking at 60%, because the multi-decade-high yield level, Japanese yields at a 1996 high and crude above $100 persist regardless of intraday structure. Confidence decays from 85% to 64% as the current price-path evidence ages across the window. The path assumes the rate-repricing regime stays unresolved but that price discovery remains orderly. Observed opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks would argue for a higher Tail than published, while a cooling bond market or a genuine two-way cash open would argue for a lower one.
